subject: BridgePipe: replacement of telemetry collector -> TelemetryHub (subprocessor change)
messages:
From: BridgePipe Support <support@bridgepipe.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Ortiz <s.ortiz@finanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Notification: Telemetry collector swap (StreamRelay -> TelemetryHub) — effective 2026-01-05

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re well — I’m reaching from BridgePipe’s Trust & Ops team to let you know we’re replacing our StreamRelay telemetry collector with TelemetryHub (v2) on 2026-01-05. This change affects the telemetry processing subcomponent that collects delivery & event traces for customers using our managed agent.

Key bullets: 
- What changes: StreamRelay (our legacy collector) will be retired; TelemetryHub will handle ingestion, enrichment and temporary buffering before forwarding to analytics backends.
- Data residency: TelemetryHub nodes will continue to run in EU regions for EU customers, but some processing (enrichment & signature checks) occurs in a minimal US staging cluster for shard reconciliation.
- Security: TelemetryHub supports AES-256 at rest and TLS1.3 in transit. We’ll continue to use customer-unique keys under BridgePipe KMS; export to US is under our subprocessor controls.

We’ve attached the official notice and a first-pass dataflow diagram. Please let us know if Redwood needs a longer attestation package (SOC 2 artifact, KMS policy excerpt, or export control declarations).

Attachments: bridgepipe-subprocessor-change-notice.pdf, telemetryhub-dataflow-diagram.v1.png

Thanks,
Marta Lira
Trust & Ops — BridgePipe
support@bridgepipe.io

--
BridgePipe, Inc.
W: https://bridgepipe.io
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: BridgePipe Support <support@bridgepipe.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notification: Telemetry collector swap (StreamRelay -> TelemetryHub) — effective 2026-01-05

Marta,

Thanks for the heads-up and the diagram — appreciate the early notice. A couple of clarifying asks from our side to complete our DPA/subprocessor review: 

1) Can you confirm whether any raw event payloads containing user identifiers (email, user_id, ip) are persisted outside EU for >24 hours? If yes, which fields and for how long?
2) Which KMS is used for EU keys? Is it BridgePipe-managed HSM or a cloud KMS (GCP/AWS/CUSTOM)? Any key export paths to US KMS?
3) Who are the chained subprocessors for TelemetryHub (e.g., cloud infra, analytics partner)? We need a roster + country list.
4) Please point us to the SOC 2 description page and any recent report you can share under NDA.

We’ll triage this via our privacy intake — tagging Kimberly for legal/compliance check and Ben for engineering impact (routing/fallback). If you can provide the answers and a redacted export-control statement by EOD Wed (2025-12-17), that would keep us on schedule for the customer onboarding we’re supporting.

Also: the dataflow diagram you attached references a US staging cluster — can you annotate which flows include PII vs telemetry-only metrics? The diagram we received isn’t labeled granularly.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

From: BridgePipe Support <support@bridgepipe.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Ortiz <s.ortiz@finanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Dec 2025 07:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notification: Telemetry collector swap (StreamRelay -> TelemetryHub) — details + attachments

Hi Irene,

Thanks — answers below and I’ve uploaded an attestation bundle to the Drive link (shared read-only). Please find the short answers here and the bundle attached on the Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3C_bridgepipe-change

1) Persistence of identifiers: TelemetryHub buffers enriched events for up to 12 hours in the EU cluster. For a subset of reconciliation shards, hashed user identifiers (HMAC) and routing metadata are held in the US staging cluster for up to 72 hours. No raw emails or plain-user identifiers are exported to the US — only hashed ids and routing metadata.

2) KMS: EU keys are stored in customer-partitioned AWS KMS keys (eu-west-1) under BridgePipe’s account with strict key policies. No key material is exported to the US. We also support customer-managed keys on request (bring-your-own-KMS).

3) Chained subprocessors: 
- Cloud infra: AWS (eu-west-1, us-east-1)
- Observability: LogDrift (processing in EU + US)
- Enrichment ML: DataForge Labs (US) — only for non-PII feature extractions (we provide hashed ids)
We’ve included a CSV roster in the Drive and country mapping in the bundle.

4) SOC 2: Redacted SOC 2 Type II summary and control narrative included in the Drive bundle (NDA required for full report).

Attachments uploaded to Drive: bridgepipe-change-bundle.zip (includes telemetryhub-dataflow-diagram.v1.png, roster.csv, soc2-summary.pdf)

Let me know if you want a short call this week to walk through the diagram — I can schedule with our compliance engineer.

Regards,
Marta Lira
Trust & Ops — BridgePipe
support@bridgepipe.io
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: BridgePipe Support <support@bridgepipe.io>
Date: Tue, 16 Dec 2025 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Notification: Telemetry collector swap (StreamRelay -> TelemetryHub) — review + proposed next steps

Kimberly / Ben,

Forwarding BridgePipe’s responses and the Drive bundle link. My read: they will continue to keep raw PII in EU, but a limited set of hashed ids and metadata flows to a US staging cluster for up to 72 hours. They claim EU KMS storage and no export of key material.

Proposed next steps: 
- Legal/Privacy (Kimberly): confirm whether hashed identifiers + 72-hour US staging buffer are acceptable under our DPA for FinAnalytics (related_account). If not, request a stricter SLA or onshore-only processing.
- Engineering (Ben): confirm whether our telemetry ingestion integrations can be configured to avoid US staging for FinAnalytics tenant (i.e., pin region to eu-west-1) and whether we can require BYOK for this customer.
- Ops: if we accept, ask BridgePipe for a signed addendum (subprocessor change addendum) and SOC2 NDA copy.

If you can circle back by EOD Thu (2025-12-18) I’ll prepare the addendum draft to send to BridgePipe. Marta — thanks again; we may request the short walkthrough depending on the legal/eng outcome.

Best,
Irene
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
